Description

Activated ERK1 and ERK2 move from the cytoplasm into the nucleus within minutes of stimulation, while their activator MEK stays in the cytoplasm. In resting cells MEK holds ERK in the cytoplasm, and ERK leaves MEK when the pathway is activated [1, 2]. A second route has been described: casein kinase 2 (CK2) phosphorylates a Ser-Pro-Ser motif in the kinase insert of active ERK (Ser246 and Ser248 in ERK2), and the phosphorylated motif binds importin 7, which carries ERK into the nucleus [3, 4]. The same motif drives the nuclear entry of other signalling proteins [3]. Other studies found entry through the pore without a carrier [5, 6].

References

  2. Burack WR, Shaw AS. Live Cell Imaging of ERK and MEK: simple binding equilibrium explains the regulated nucleocytoplasmic distribution of ERK. J Biol Chem. 2005;280(5):3832-7. PMID: 15546878. doi: 10.1074/jbc.M410031200.
  3. Chuderland D, Konson A, Seger R. Identification and characterization of a general nuclear translocation signal in signaling proteins. Mol Cell. 2008;31(6):850-61. PMID: 18760948. doi: 10.1016/j.molcel.2008.08.007.
  4. Plotnikov A, Chuderland D, Karamansha Y, Livnah O, Seger R. Nuclear ERK Translocation is Mediated by Protein Kinase CK2 and Accelerated by Autophosphorylation. Cell Physiol Biochem. 2019;53(2):366-387. PMID: 31385665. doi: 10.33594/000000144.
